sections.title: Profile
sections.text: Software engineer building LLM agent pipelines that process 20,000+ wholesale orders daily at Canals AI, a U.S.-based AI company for the industrial supply chain. Summa cum laude graduate in Systems and Computing Engineering with the program’s highest GPA in 40 years (4.92/5.00) and current adjunct professor of algorithm design at Universidad de los Andes.

schools.name: Universidad de los Andes
schools.degree: B.Sc. in Systems and Computing Engineering
bullets: Summa cum laude: top 1% of School of Engineering graduates by GPA, selected after a committee interview
GPA: 4.92/5.00, the highest in the program in 40 years and in the School of Engineering in 16 years
Recipient of the Quiero Estudiar Scholarship (95% tuition coverage) for the duration of the degree

roles.title: Software Engineer II
bullets: Own the parsing services for the live voice and inquiry agent systems, part of a pipeline that processes 20,000+ orders daily across 115+ wholesale distributors and 9,000+ sales reps, and maintain a 481-case end-to-end regression suite

Built the parsing and review layers of a real-time voice service (WebSocket orchestration, speech-to-text, speaker diarization, concurrency control). Extracted about 21 products per live phone call, with 75%+ retained through rep review

Integrated tools (web search, spec sheet retrieval, ERP lookup, order tracking) into an AI inquiry agent that addressed customer questions about orders, materials, and logistics. Achieved source citations in 97% of answers and positive rep ratings on 80%

Contributed to Canals’ shared agent framework (Mastra), adding support for extended thinking, reasoning effort, image/PDF input, temperature, and tool concurrency. Migrated four parsing agents from hand-rolled, unbounded loops to bounded runs with step and token ceilings
Co-built an autonomous agent (Claude Agent SDK) that polled tickets, debugged parsing failures, and shipped prompt-level fixes, re-parsing each order to verify its own fix

roles.title: Software Engineer I
bullets: Maintained a parsing pipeline supporting 19 MIME types with intricate formats (e.g., handwritten and struck-through text, blurry and fragmented photos, cross-references to other files), serving about 60 wholesale distributors that processed 4,000+ orders daily

Abstracted the OCR pipeline from a single provider to support multiple providers, decoupling the implementation from Textract and enabling format-specific OCR selection across 18.2 million documents, with a cache layer serving about 60% of requests in 0.07 s versus 3.6–18.7 s uncached
Led large-scale prompt refactors spanning model selection, prompt engineering, cache handling, and regression testing, improving the external QA pass rate from 85% to 89%
Built visual highlighting systems using DOM traversal, coordinate mapping, and string comparison to map parsed products to source documents. Reduced weekly highlighting errors by two-thirds

roles.title: Full-Stack Developer
bullets: Designed and built a full-stack student data analytics system serving 15,000+ students and 600+ faculty, replacing an external platform and saving about US$100,000 annually
Built a parallelized data-processing pipeline (Python, Polars) with complex filtering and aggregations, exposed through a unified REST API (FastAPI)
Developed dynamic graphing, advanced filtering, report generation, and role-based dashboards in a React/TypeScript web application
Built an early-warning system for at-risk students (academic performance, dropout indicators), alerting counselors to 1,000+ critical cases
Architected secure communication between VMs, isolating the machine holding student data on a segmented network to ensure compliance with student data protection requirements

roles.title: Software Developer I
bullets: Developed Python-based Jupyter notebooks for financial and auditing data analysis
Optimized the performance of Java and TypeScript microservices using Amazon S3 and DynamoDB, identifying and resolving bugs
Authored and delivered technical reports (spikes, RFCs) that influenced team architecture decisions and established best practices
Awarded the June Team Award for “delivering impactful contributions and hard work” as part of the Data Analytics team

roles.title: Backend Developer
bullets: Designed and implemented the backend architecture for the Professors’ Portfolio system (Java, Spring Boot), a web application for managing faculty academic and administrative information
Built persistence, logic, and control layers with CRUD operations, custom logic, and RESTful APIs
Devised efficient data migration methods to store large volumes of unstructured faculty data in relational databases
Collaborated with Prof. José Bocanegra, Ph.D., on system architecture documentation and technical specifications, contributing to project planning and implementation roadmaps

roles.title: Adjunct Professor
roles.subtitle: Algorithm Design
bullets: Principal instructor for an upper-division algorithm design course, lecturing and designing exams
Topics: divide and conquer, dynamic programming, graph algorithms, NP-completeness, approximation and randomized algorithms

roles.title: Adjunct Professor
roles.subtitle: Introduction to Programming
bullets: Principal instructor for an introductory undergraduate course in procedural programming using Python
Topics: programming fundamentals and the data-processing libraries pandas and Matplotlib

roles.title: Undergraduate Research Teaching Assistant
roles.subtitle: CupiTaller
bullets: Collaborated on a seven-person team to manage the university’s programming support center
Oversaw the university’s Coursera courses “Programming in Python” and “Introduction to Object Oriented Programming in Java,” with 50,000+ and 60,000+ historical enrollments, respectively

Designed and co-built CupiHorarios, a scheduling web application (FastAPI, React) leveraging the Pyomo optimization modeling library to generate schedules that ensured full coverage during operating hours

Co-designed and co-built CupiFeedback, a tutoring performance analytics web application (FastAPI, React) that collected feedback from 1,500+ students and presented insights through interactive visualizations
